Live bonds

Live from Monad testnet via Envio. Dollar totals use the deployment’s USDC; counts include all indexed accounts. Collected means revenue sent to bond pools, not holder redemptions. Demo businesses and traffic are run by the Bondrail team.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

Live from Monad testnet via Envio. Dollar totals use the deployment’s USDC; counts include all indexed accounts. Collected means revenue sent to bond pools, not holder redemptions. Demo businesses and traffic are run by the Bondrail team.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

Live bonds

Live from Monad testnet via Envio. Dollar totals use the deployment’s USDC; counts include all indexed accounts. Collected means revenue sent to bond pools, not holder redemptions. Demo businesses and traffic are run by the Bondrail team.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

Live bonds

Live from Monad testnet via Envio. Dollar totals use the deployment’s USDC; counts include all indexed accounts. Collected means revenue sent to bond pools, not holder redemptions. Demo businesses and traffic are run by the Bondrail team.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

Live bonds

Live from Monad testnet via Envio. Dollar totals use the deployment’s USDC; counts include all indexed accounts. Collected means revenue sent to bond pools, not holder redemptions. Demo businesses and traffic are run by the Bondrail team.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched

Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

Live bonds

Live from Monad testnet via Envio. Dollar totals use the deployment’s USDC; counts include all indexed accounts. Collected means revenue sent to bond pools, not holder redemptions. Demo businesses and traffic are run by the Bondrail team.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

Live bonds

Live from Monad testnet via Envio. Dollar totals use the deployment’s USDC; counts include all indexed accounts. Collected means revenue sent to bond pools, not holder redemptions. Demo businesses and traffic are run by the Bondrail team.

(01) How it works

From revenue to a funded bond.

Record revenue, set the terms, and let investors assess the business behind the bond.

(01)

Open an account

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.

Create a revenue account in the token you earn. It is your revenue address from day one.

(02)

Build history

Native fees and account settlements prove a payer on-chain. Plain transfers are booked by sweep without a proven payer.

(03)

Issue a bond

Set the bond terms against your revenue history. Investors fund it; 25% or 50% is released, the rest at a milestone.

(04)

Route revenue to repayment

The current revenue share goes toward repayment, up to the cap. Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers still need sweep.

(02) Two tiers

Routing enforced in code, or monitored.
Native
Built on Bondrail

A reviewed template or individually reviewed project routes fees through its bound account using BondrailEarner. Review covers the disclosed code path; it does not guarantee future business revenue.

· collect() for money in, settleOut() for money out
· payer proven by the transfer itself
· optional fee floor while a bond is live
Read the guide
Watched
Paid APIs over x402

Your API pays its account. Chainlink CRE checks every paid endpoint every 30 minutes; a confirmed diversion defaults the bond and slashes your stake.

· /.well-known/bondrail.json manifest
· every payment option must pay the account
· guarded buyers verify payTo before paying
Read the guide

(03) For builders

Start the record today.

Route revenue through an account. Build history, then set terms investors can assess.

Build with the npm packages @bondrail/sdk and @bondrail/contracts.

Quickstart

(04) For investors

Underwrite evidence, not promises.

Assess attributed revenue, payer concentration and coverage. Buy claims on Kuru where listed, or fund a raise. Early redemption burns claims for current backing and gives up future receipts.

Pool capital in the credit vault, inspect credit profiles, and check performance triggers that can raise the investor share when revenue falls.

Browse markets
Browse markets

(05) Trust

Every assumption, disclosed.

Read the full trust model in the docs.

(01)
Who can stop the split?

Native fees and x402 payments settled through BondrailAccount.settle via the Bondrail facilitator split in the same transaction. Plain transfers split when anyone calls sweep. Revoking Native project or template approval blocks new deposits and releases unless another approval still applies; repayment of a live bond continues.

(02)
What do I rely on?

A disclosed Native reviewer approves projects or templates; a milestone signer approves signed milestones where selected; observer reports arrive through Chainlink CRE. Signed credit assessments rely on the attester, and vault allocations rely on the curator within contract limits.

(03)
What if the business stops?

Revenue stops too. Holders retain the collected pool and undrawn capital when it is recovered. Watched stake goes to investors only on a recorded default. Coverage and any available Kuru price help assess risk; neither guarantees repayment.

(04)
Can revenue be faked?

Self-payments still pay the investor share while a bond collects revenue. Indexer attribution excludes detected issuer-linked payers and plain transfers, but cannot prove customer independence. Performance triggers use all booked revenue, including self-payments.

(05)
Is this live?

On Monad testnet, with team-run demo businesses and traffic. The contracts are not audited.
